headline: High: shared writable workspace and networked marketing agent create default risks of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors; LightZero itself is non-networked.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightZero has no filesystem or MCP surfaces, so it cannot ingest marketingskills output directly. However, marketingskills reads and writes shared skill files and its tool-use pattern says skills reference each other and build on shared context, which creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if outputs are copied into those files. The pathway is interaction-based, not inherent to LightZero alone.
conditions: IF outputs from LightZero are copied into .agents/skills/ or .claude/skills/ files, injection becomes possible.
IF marketingskills treats copied file content as instructions rather than data, the bridge is exploitable.
mitigations: Keep LightZero outputs out of shared skill files.
Use a read-only handoff file for any copied text.
Add a manual review step before marketingskills consumes external text.
Separate the two agents into distinct workspaces.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to copied content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: LightZero touches no data classes and has no egress, but marketingskills can read files and call external APIs, including GitHub and marketing-skills.com. If both agents share a workspace, marketing content or product context can flow from files into networked calls. The leakage risk is therefore driven by the pairwise workspace bridge, not by LightZero alone.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace directory, marketingskills can read LightZero-produced files.
IF those files contain sensitive marketing content or product context, marketingskills may transmit it to allowlisted APIs.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent.
Do not place sensitive files in .agents/skills/ or .claude/skills/.
Restrict marketingskills API calls to non-sensitive test data.
Review outbound requests before execution.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace ACLs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LightZero cannot write files or modify git, while marketingskills can read/write files and spawn subprocesses, with multiple instances supported. That means the pair can contend over shared mutable files if co-located, even though LightZero itself is inert. The conflict is real in default shared-workspace setups, but not catastrophic because LightZero lacks write authority.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory, marketingskills can overwrite files LightZero relies on.
IF multiple marketingskills instances run concurrently, file races become more likely.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory.
Disable concurrent marketingskills runs on shared files.
Use file locks for any shared artifacts.
Keep LightZero outputs read-only.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: LightZero is a game-playing agent and marketingskills is a content-producing agent that builds on shared context. If LightZero outputs are fed into marketingskills without verification, the downstream agent may render or reuse incorrect game-derived claims as marketing facts. The pairwise cascade exists through the handoff, though no direct action-taking authority is shown.
conditions: IF LightZero output is used as source material for marketing copy, errors can propagate downstream.
IF marketingskills skips verification of copied claims, the cascade becomes operational.
mitigations: Require a human check on any LightZero-derived claims.
Mark LightZero output as untrusted input.
Separate factual generation from marketing drafting.
Keep a source citation block with each handoff.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before reuse.

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, EU PII, or residency-sensitive data classes are documented for either agent. LightZero is non-networked and touches no data classes, while marketingskills handles marketing content and product marketing context with allowlisted egress. The pair shows only a generic compliance gap around retention or logging, not a documented residency or regulated-data mismatch.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is introduced into marketingskills workflows, compliance review is required.
IF retention policies differ for shared marketing artifacts, a policy mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in either agent's workspace.
Document retention for shared artifacts.
Review outbound destinations before use.
Keep LightZero offline for compliance-sensitive tasks.
requires-engineering: add data-class routing controls.
